title: Telemetry incident replay and tenant-scoped redaction controls
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem: When investigating incidents we frequently need to replay traces and correlated logs. Raw telemetry can contain tenant PII (user identifiers, prompt fragments) and our current pipeline lacks fine-grained controls for redaction, differential retention, and auditable access during incident investigations.

Goal: Implement a tenant-scoped telemetry replay workflow that allows (a) safe replay of traces/logs for debugging, (b) deterministic and configurable PII redaction before long-term storage, and (c) just-in-time unredaction under RBAC with full access logging and approval metadata. The feature must preserve low latency for normal inference flows (target runtime overhead <2%) and integrate with existing tracing hooks and metrics pipelines.

Scope: tracing spans, request/response logs, debug snapshots (KV cache dumps), and related metrics labels. Out-of-scope for this ticket: raw customer payload archival outside retention window, long-term analytics pipelines that require separate approval and SSO gating.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic redaction layer exists that can be applied at ingestion (span/log) and at replay-time with the same rule set
Per-tenant retention TTLs configurable via Console and enforced by pipeline (min/soft-max bounds)
RBAC-protected replay endpoint: only authorized roles can request unredacted replay; every unredaction action emits an access log with approver, justification, and timestamp
Replay flow can operate on sampled or full traces depending on incident severity; sampling config is tenant-aware and stored in config service
End-to-end benchmark shows <2% added p99 latency for on-path telemetry enrichment with redaction checks enabled
Integration tests covering scrubber correctness for 12 representative PII patterns and automated regression checks added to CI
implementation_notes: Design a two-stage scrubber: fast on-path scrub (regex/token-strip of high-risk fields) + offline deep-scrub for long-term storage using model-assisted classifiers
Annotate spans with a data-class label to control downstream retention and scrubber aggressiveness
Introduce a 'replay-ticket' object in the control plane that records justification, approver, TTL for unredaction, and links to GitHub PR or incident timeline
Leverage existing trace ingestion hooks (trace-enrich service) to add tenant_id, sampled flag, and data_class labels without blocking request path
Store minimal encrypted blobs for replay that are tenant-scoped and rotated with KMS; just-in-time decryption requires a short-lived grant
Provide a Console UI mock for operations to request replay with approval flow (separate PM/design ticket will own detailed UX)
risks_and_tradeoffs: On-path redaction must be conservative to avoid leaking PII; conservative scrubbing increases signal loss for debugging
Deep-scrub model-assisted step adds cost and complexity; will run offline on a best-effort basis to reduce latency impact
Just-in-time unredaction creates a higher blast radius if RBAC/approval process is misconfigured; need strict guardrails and monitoring
Sampling decisions can make incident troubleshooting harder if relevant traces are dropped — provide emergency full-capture mode per tenant
tasks: Spec: finalize scrubber rule set and data classification matrix (Confluence)
PoC: implement fast on-path scrubber in trace-enrich (optional feature flag)
Encrypt-and-store: add replay blob store with KMS integration and short-lived grants
RBAC: extend Console authz to include replay approvals and integrate with audit-log pipeline
CI: add unit + integration tests for scrubber and replay flow
Bench: run latency and cost benchmarks and validate <2% p99 overhead
